reason: Paper directly studies PROS1 as a ligand for MERTK and Tyro3 receptors, with MERTK KO mice explicitly used to dissect the pathway. Core MERTK biology; clearly on-topic for an ophthalmogenetics library studying MERTK-associated retinal dystrophy.

Review of apoptotic cell recognition and phagocytic clearance, covering phosphatidylserine recognition and immune suppression by phagocytes - the exact mechanism by which RPE cells (via MERTK) clear shed photoreceptor outer segments. Mechanistically central to MERTK biology in the retina even without explicit eye focus.

Paper is specifically about MERTK (Mer) in nephrotoxic serum-induced nephritis. The clinical context is entirely renal inflammation. While MERTK is the gene of interest, the ophthalmogenetics library should capture papers relevant to ophthalmic manifestations; a kidney-disease-specific study does not add meaningfully to understanding MERTK-related retinal dystrophy.

WldS is a fusion protein whose enzymatic component is NMNAT1; the paper directly studies WldS/NMNAT1-mediated neuroprotection in retinal ganglion cells in a glaucoma model, testing anterograde axon transport and spatial acuity. Directly on-topic for NMNAT1 and retinal neuroprotection.

Paper demonstrates that plasma extracellular vesicles trigger MERTK-dependent signaling via GAS6 and PROS1 ligands to regulate macrophage activation and neutrophil function. MERTK is explicitly and centrally studied. Provides mechanistic understanding of MERTK signaling relevant to its role in RPE phagocytosis and retinal disease.

Paper directly studies NRL in photoreceptor cell specification in zebrafish, demonstrating that Tbx2b represses synergistic Nrl/Crx activity at the rhodopsin promoter. NRL is a central subject of the study; clearly on-topic for an ophthalmogenetics library.

Review of genetic variants associated with POAG in Indian populations, with CYP1B1 and MYOC among the primary genes discussed. Published in Genomics, specifically about ophthalmic genetics of glaucoma. Directly relevant to both listed genes.

Systematic review in Survey of Ophthalmology specifically examining gene polymorphisms associated with POAG progression, with MYOC (MYOC.mt1+) explicitly identified as associated with faster optic nerve head damage and visual field deterioration. Directly on-topic for MYOC and glaucoma.

Review focuses entirely on inner ear gene therapies for hereditary hearing loss and cochlear implants. While CLRN1 and WHRN are Usher syndrome genes with both auditory and retinal phenotypes, this paper addresses only the auditory side and makes no reference to retinal disease or gene therapy for the eye. Off-topic for an ophthalmogenetics library.

Paper demonstrates AAV-mediated gene therapy restoring synaptic architecture, retinal ERG responses, and visual acuity in a mouse model of CSNB (CACNA2D4 KO). The paper is squarely about retinal gene therapy for inherited retinal disease, the primary domain of the ophthalmogenetics library. Tagged under CACNA1F/CEP290/LRIT3 as related CSNB/retinal disease genes.

Paper evaluates deep intronic variants causing cryptic exon activation in patients with recessive inherited retinal disease, testing 640 DIVs from 76 IRD patients using a high-throughput splicing assay. Directly about IRD genetics involving CLRN1, RP2, and RPGRIP1 - all retinal dystrophy genes. Clearly on-topic.

Paper is about de novo variants in spliceosomal snRNA genes (RNU4-2, RNU5B-1, RNU5A-1) causing neurodevelopmental disorders (ReNU syndrome). No ophthalmic phenotype is described; the disorder and study focus are entirely neurological/developmental. The gene_or_topic RNU2-2 appears to be a peripheral keyword match rather than the paper's subject.

Classic paper on choroidal thickness changes and scleral compensation in chick myopia/emmetropization. Directly studies choroidal biology relevant to the Middle coat anatomy category and ARR3 myopia gene context. Core literature for ocular growth regulation.

Paper directly studies the CRYbetaA1-DeltaG91 mutation causing autosomal dominant congenital nuclear cataract in mice, examining crystallin gene expression, protein insolubilization, and lens epithelial cell changes. CRYBA1 is the primary subject; CRYAA, CRYBB2, CRYBB3 are related crystallin genes also discussed. Directly on-topic.

Paper studies gamma-D crystallin (CRYGD) stability under crowded conditions mimicking the human eye lens cytoplasm. Directly relevant to lens biology and understanding crystallin protein behavior associated with CRYGD/CRYAA/CRYBA4 mutations causing cataract.

Paper is specifically about TENM3 (Teneurin-3) controlling topographic circuit assembly in the hippocampus (CA1-subiculum-entorhinal cortex connectivity). The abstract briefly notes TENM3 is 'required for vertebrate visual system development' as background, but the entire study is in the hippocampus with no ophthalmic data. Not relevant to microphthalmia or eye disease.

Paper characterizes expression of the four Ten-m/Odz (Teneurin) genes in the developing and adult mouse brain. No reference to eye, visual system, retina, or ophthalmic phenotype. Brain expression atlas study; not relevant to the ophthalmogenetics library.

Paper dissects the structural organization and activation mechanisms of gamma-TuRCs in centrosomes, with TUBGCP4 (GCP4) as a component. TUBGCP4 is associated with microphthalmia and retinal dystrophy; understanding its molecular function in gamma-TuRC is mechanistic background relevant to interpreting TUBGCP4-linked eye disease. Centrosome/cilia biology is frequently pertinent to ophthalmic ciliopathies.

Classic paper describing genetic heterogeneity in blue-cone monochromacy, characterizing OPN1LW and OPN1MW gene rearrangements (locus control region deletions, homologous recombination, point mutations) as causes. Directly relevant to multiple listed genes (CNGA3, OPN1LW, OPN1MW) and the retinal dystrophies topic category.

Paper clones and characterizes CNG-3 (CNGA3) from bovine kidney as a cyclic nucleotide-gated channel family member. The abstract explicitly opens by noting CNG channels are essential for visual signal transduction. CNGA3 mutations cause achromatopsia; this is a foundational characterization paper for the gene, clearly relevant to the ophthalmogenetics library.
